context: Extract the geometry-bearing class strings into shared constants used by both the loaded and skeleton render paths, so parity is structural rather than asserted by a test comparing two literals. A test that compares only one pair of strings would certify an incomplete fix, and strict whole-subtree equality is wrong because the loaded hero renders ActiveLeaderboardSummary which the skeleton does not.
description: Home.tsx carries comments stating that the skeleton hero mirrors the loaded hero exactly, because earlier drift caused visible reflow when data arrived. Below 640px they no longer match. Loaded hero wrapper :360 is 'px-4 py-4 sm:px-6 sm:py-7 lg:px-8 lg:py-4' against skeleton :607 'px-4 py-7 sm:px-6 lg:px-8 lg:py-4'. Loaded headline :362 is 'text-2xl font-bold sm:text-4xl' against skeleton :609 'text-3xl font-bold sm:text-4xl'. Loaded data surface :478 is 'py-4 sm:py-8' against skeleton :634 'py-8'. A third drift the first audit missed - loaded ranking selector :383 is 'mt-3 p-2 sm:mt-5 sm:p-3' with 'grid-cols-2 gap-2 sm:gap-3' against skeleton :620 'mt-5 p-3' with 'gap-3'. So at mobile widths the headline shrinks 30px to 24px and the hero loses padding the moment data lands. There is NO test asserting this parity, only prose comments - which is precisely why it regressed. Verified at HEAD 39ead3a41.

anti_patterns.dont: Assert the skeleton and loaded subtrees are identical
anti_patterns.why: the loaded hero renders ActiveLeaderboardSummary and the skeleton deliberately does not
